title: Vienna Rising
premise: Oscar Montrose, a private security contractor who protects clients the intelligence world disavows, receives a calendar invite from her dead handler, Nadia Kessler, scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at 9 a.m. in Vienna. The invitation is a dead-man's-switch message from the network that trained Oscar herself — a deniable asset pipeline called the Meridian Group — now cleaning house before a whistleblower surfaces. Pursued by former colleagues and shadowed by a young runaway, Ilse, who carries the proof Nadia died protecting, Oscar must decide whether loyalty to the people who made her outweighs the truth they buried. In the end she burns Meridian's Vienna cell from the inside, exposes its patron in a public reckoning she may not survive, and walks away from the trade entirely, choosing the fragile found family she built over the legend she was trained to be.
about_author: Wren Halloran is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for private security firms across Central Europe. Vienna Rising is their third novel and the first to trade directly on that past.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Oscar Montrose finishes a quiet extraction job in Bratislava and returns to Vienna to find a calendar invite on her secure account from Nadia Kessler — her handler, dead for six weeks. The meeting is set for 9 a.m. tomorrow. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional calm, the first crack in her controlled world.

chapters.title: Clients Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter establishing Oscar's trade: guarding a paranoid fintech executive who pays in cash and secrets. Her colleague Tomas teases her about her hermit life; her apartment is a fortress with one photo of her training cohort. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline, the cost of a life built on discretion.

chapters.title: Nine A.M., Karlsplatz
chapters.summary: Oscar goes to the meeting point anyway, telling herself it's reconnaissance. Instead of Nadia, she finds a dead drop: a burner phone, a photograph of a training facility she swore she'd forgotten, and a countdown. Someone watches from the crowd and vanishes. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose — someone is using Nadia's death to reach her.

chapters.title: The Girl on the U-Bahn
chapters.summary: Following the phone's only contact, Oscar spots a teenage girl, Ilse, being followed by two professionals on the U4. Ilse clutches a battered laptop bag like a lifeline. Oscar intervenes with brutal efficiency and gets them both clear. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: reluctant protectiveness awakening; the first bond she hasn't vetted.

chapters.title: What Ilse Carries
chapters.summary: In a safehouse, Ilse reveals she was Nadia's courier — the laptop holds Meridian Group ledgers: names, payments, and a training program that manufactured deniable assets. Oscar recognizes her own file number. POV: Oscar, with Ilse's fragmented testimony. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past she buried is the case she's holding.

chapters.title: The Meridian Method
chapters.summary: Oscar decrypts enough of the archive to confirm the pipeline that recruited her at nineteen still operates, now selling loyalty tests that end in disappearances. Nadia's name appears in the margins as a marked informant. POV: Oscar, reading. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into fury; the mentors were the monsters.

chapters.title: Old Cohort
chapters.summary: Oscar contacts Marcus Vey, the only other surviving member of her training cohort, now a respected security consultant. Their reunion is warm until she notices he's asking the wrong questions about her location. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the ache of testing an old friend and hating herself for it.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: A quiet interlude: Oscar teaches Ilse tradecraft basics — countersurveillance, cover stories, how to lie calmly. Ilse's sharpness unsettles Oscar; she sees her younger self. POV: alternating Oscar and Ilse. Emotional beat: found family forming in the negative space of danger, tenderness disguised as instruction.

chapters.title: The Cleaner Arrives
chapters.summary: Meridian's fixer, a methodical man called Anselm Roth, arrives in Vienna and begins erasing Nadia's network — a forger, a banker, a landlady, each death staged as accident. Oscar reads the pattern in the news and realizes the clock is real. POV: Roth, cold and procedural, with a coda from Oscar. Emotional beat: dread; the enemy is patient and professional.

chapters.title: Tomas's Debt
chapters.summary: Oscar pulls Tomas into the case for logistics, breaking her own rule about involving civilians. He owes her from a job gone wrong in Sarajevo and agrees without asking questions she can't answer. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: loyalty freely given, and Oscar's guilt at spending it.

chapters.title: The Banker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar and Tomas intercept the banker before Roth does, extracting a second ledger linking Meridian to a senior Austrian intelligence official, Deputy Director Konrad Falk. The trail now points upward. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the case outgrows revenge — this is systemic, and exposure means powerful enemies.

chapters.title: Vey's Warning
chapters.summary: Marcus Vey warns Oscar to walk away, claiming Meridian is beyond burning and that Nadia knew the risk. His concern reads as care but lands as a threat. After he leaves, Oscar finds a tracker in her coat. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: heartbreak — the cohort's loyalty was always conditional.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Oscar burns her identities, moves Ilse twice, and adopts a tradecraft she hasn't used since training: becoming no one. Ilse struggles with the erasure of her own name. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: the terror and strange freedom of disappearing; identity as a thing you can lose.

chapters.title: Nadia's Apartment
chapters.summary: Oscar breaks into Nadia's sealed Vienna apartment and finds a hidden drive: Nadia's own confession — she'd been feeding evidence to a journalist, Lena Brandt, who vanished three weeks ago. Nadia died buying time. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance; she's carrying two dead women's work now.

chapters.title: The Journalist's Trail
chapters.summary: Oscar traces Lena Brandt to a farmhouse in Lower Austria where the journalist is held, not dead — Meridian wants her source list. Oscar cases the site and finds it guarded by training-cohort graduates. People she ate with, trained with. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the horror of recognizing your own reflection in the men you must kill.

chapters.title: Farmhouse
chapters.summary: The rescue goes wrong: Oscar frees Brandt but is recognized by a cohort graduate, Petra Lang, who hesitates — and lets her go. Roth notices the hesitation. POV: Oscar, then Roth. Emotional beat: a crack in Meridian's loyalty machine; mercy as the first act of rebellion.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brandt, half-broken, reveals her story runs in forty-eight hours with or without Oscar — but Meridian's patron, Falk, can kill it. She needs the ledgers authenticated and a source on record. Oscar must decide to go public. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: the weight of truth as a weapon that wounds its wielder first.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Roth interrogates Petra Lang about the farmhouse failure. She covers for Oscar, and Roth executes her for it — quietly, as a training accident. POV: Roth, with a final image of Petra's file being closed. Emotional beat: cold rage in the reader; the machine consumes its own.

chapters.title: The Trap Vey Built
chapters.summary: Oscar meets Vey at a Danube restaurant to force a choice: help or be exposed. He chooses Meridian, tipping Roth to her location. The dinner becomes a silent duel; Oscar leaves first and survives the ambush he arranged. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the death of the last illusion about her old family.

chapters.title: Ilse Runs
chapters.summary: Fearing she's the liability, Ilse takes the laptop and runs to trade it for her own safety, contacting a fixer who is Roth's asset. She realizes the trap too late. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: fear and self-blame; a child learning that the world punishes trust.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Roth holds Ilse and offers Oscar a trade: the ledgers and Brandt's silence for the girl. Oscar agrees — and comes to the exchange with a plan Roth doesn't know she has, using Tomas's logistics and Meridian's own protocols against it. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: terror and resolve; she will not trade the family she found for the truth she owes.

chapters.title: Counterweight
chapters.summary: The exchange at a freight depot turns violent. Oscar's counter-ambush frees Ilse and wounds Roth, but Tomas is captured covering the escape, and the second ledger is lost. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: victory with a bill attached; every win costs a piece of someone.

chapters.title: Roth's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV shift into Roth: recovering, he reviews the depot operation and finds the flaw in his own thinking — Oscar fights like Meridian trained her, which means he can predict her. He sets a final trap keyed to her instincts. Emotional beat: the hunter's cold clarity; the pupil's patterns are her cage.

chapters.title: Falk's Parlor
chapters.summary: Deputy Director Konrad Falk hosts a discreet gathering where Meridian's patrons toast the network's renewal. Vey attends, hollow-eyed. Falk announces the whistleblower problem will be resolved this week. POV: Falk. Emotional beat: banal evil in good tailoring; the reader sees the summit Oscar must storm.

chapters.title: The Third Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar realizes Nadia kept a third copy — the authentication Brandt needs — hidden in the one place Meridian would never search: the training facility itself, decommissioned but intact in the Vienna Woods. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grim irony; the house that made her keeps the evidence of its crimes.

chapters.title: Return to the House
chapters.summary: Oscar and Ilse infiltrate the derelict facility. Walking its corridors, Oscar's memories surface in fragments — the recruitment, the loyalty tests, the girl she was. They find Nadia's cache in the old evaluation room. POV: Oscar, memory-bleed. Emotional beat: confrontation with the self Meridian manufactured.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Facility
chapters.summary: Roth's trap springs — he predicted she'd come home. Ilse executes her training under fire, saving them both, and they escape through the forest with the third ledger. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: the student surpassing the curriculum; found family proving stronger than forged loyalty.

chapters.title: Authentication
chapters.summary: Brandt verifies the ledgers against her source material: the story is airtight, naming Falk, Meridian, and the program — and, in a footnote, Oscar's own file. Publication is set for dawn. POV: Brandt and Oscar. Emotional beat: the point of no return; truth once printed cannot be unmade.

chapters.title: Tomas, Traded
chapters.summary: Oscar locates Tomas in a Meridian holding site and trades the location of a Meridian asset in Prague to get him out. Tomas, freed and furious, insists on staying in the fight. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: loyalty repaid and doubled; the crew is now all-in.

chapters.title: Vey's Confession
chapters.summary: Vey, unraveling, meets Oscar one last time and confesses he reported Nadia's informant status to save himself. He gives her Falk's private schedule for the next day — the Vienna Intelligence Gala — then asks her not to forgive him. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: guilt as the only loyalty left; a traitor's gift.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: the safehouse, guns cleaned, Brandt's draft read aloud. Ilse asks Oscar what happens after; Oscar answers honestly that she doesn't know. Tomas cooks. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the calm before, and the discovery that this ragged group has become the thing she was trained never to need.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Oscar enters the Vienna Intelligence Gala under a borrowed identity, Vey's schedule in hand, while Tomas runs countersurveillance and Ilse monitors comms. Falk works the room, untouchable in plain sight. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the predator walking into the herd; controlled fury behind a smile.

chapters.title: Confrontation
chapters.summary: Oscar corners Falk in a private study with the ledgers' contents and a dead-man's-switch set to publish everything — including his personal file — unless he stands down. Falk calls her bluff by ordering Roth to take Brandt. POV: Oscar and Falk. Emotional beat: the duel of leverage; truth versus institutional power.

chapters.title: Roth Moves
chapters.summary: Roth's team hits the safehouse for Brandt. Tomas and Ilse execute the fallback plan, moving Brandt through Vienna's sewers and service tunnels while Roth closes in. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: terror and competence; the found family fighting for its own without its leader.

chapters.title: The Riesenrad
chapters.summary: Oscar lures Roth to the Prater and ends it on the Riesenrad's platform — not with an execution, but by leaving him for the police with the evidence of his own murders, a cruelty he never trained for: consequence. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, but justice nonetheless; mercy as a weapon.

chapters.title: Dawn Edition
chapters.summary: Brandt's story publishes: Meridian exposed, Falk named, the program documented. Falk is arrested within hours; the network's patrons scatter. Vey's name appears in the reporting as a cooperating source. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: the world tilting toward light; truth landing like weather, indifferent and total.

chapters.title: Loose Threads
chapters.summary: Meridian's remnants offer Oscar a partnership — the network survives its patrons, and they know her value. She declines and sends the offer, verbatim, to Brandt. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the final severance; she chooses to burn the bridge behind her.

chapters.title: What the Training Made
chapters.summary: Oscar dismantles her arsenal, closes her accounts, and reads her own Meridian file one last time before burning it. Ilse watches, understanding she's witnessing a funeral. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: mourning the self she was built to be; identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The New Address
chapters.summary: Weeks later: a small flat without fortifications, Tomas fixing the boiler, Brandt visiting with proofs of her book, Ilse enrolled in school under a name Oscar helped her choose. Nadia's photo finally joins the one from the training cohort. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: found family at rest; the ordinary as hard-won prize.

chapters.title: Vienna Rising
chapters.summary: Oscar takes one last walk at dawn — past Karlsplatz, the depot, the Prater — and feels the city as a place she chose rather than a map she worked. A stranger asks for directions; she gives them, plainly, and keeps walking. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: quiet resurrection; the woman outlived the weapon.
